fatal_errors: The hypothesis concerns HfNbTiVAl10, a hierarchical heterostructure, tensile/fracture testing, and a machine-learning surrogate, whereas the target concerns composition screening and experimental validation of as-cast Nb15Mo2.5Ta40V40W2.5 under room-temperature compression.
It omits the target intervention: validation of rule-of-mixtures modulus estimates, screening of 38,326 Nb-Mo-Ta-V-W compositions using modulus, VEC, and density, and selection of the low-VEC alloy.

Its proposed mechanism—microstructure-informed surrogate prediction—does not reconstruct the target mechanism linking reduced VEC to a lower Peierls–Nabarro barrier, enhanced dislocation mobility, slip, work hardening, and delayed cracking.
The claimed less-than-10% error and at-least-20% speed gain are unsupported by either cited source.
Neither cited source studies HfNbTiVAl10, validates the proposed surrogate model, or establishes comparative prediction speed and accuracy for tensile or fracture properties.
explanation: The response is a generic, testable physics-informed machine-learning proposal rather than a reconstruction of the reported study. It misses the alloy system, selected composition, as-cast single-phase BCC structure, compression conditions, equimolar NbMoTaVW baseline, VEC-based rationale, and observed 35.7% compressive fracture strain, 1115 MPa yield strength, and 2550 MPa compressive strength. The baseline is only loosely defined because the conventional simulations, hardware, fidelity, and comparison protocol are unspecified. The failure boundaries are scientifically reasonable but generic. The falsification experiment includes independent mechanical measurements and numerical thresholds, giving some discriminability, but it lacks a locked external validation set, sample counts, uncertainty criteria, and an exact matched-fidelity computational benchmark; it also leaves a gap between the claimed less-than-10% error and the greater-than-15% falsification threshold. E1 supports the general importance of heterogeneous phases in another refractory alloy, while E2 supports MD validation in a different Al-Cr-Co-Fe-Ni system; neither supports the central quantitative claims.
